records.text: On 2023-05-29, the user asked for more detailed, practical examples of Next.js 13.2 `generateStaticParams`, preferably using a free API.

On 2023-05-29, the assistant began a practical Next.js App Router example using the free JSONPlaceholder API (`https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts`). It proposed `app/blog/[postId]/page.tsx`, fetching all posts in `generateStaticParams` and returning string `postId` values, then fetching an individual post from `/posts/${params.postId}`. It also began an `app/posts/page.tsx` listing page linking to `/blog/${post.id}`. The assistant's example incorrectly suggested custom data returned by `generateMetadata` would be passed as props to the page; the response was cut off while showing the post-list metadata fetch.

On 2023-05-29, the assistant continued a Next.js 13.2 `generateStaticParams` example using JSONPlaceholder. The assistant showed fetching `https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts`, parsing the response as posts, and mapping each post to an object containing its numeric `id` and `title`.

On 2023-05-29, the assistant incorrectly claimed that `generateMetadata` for a `/posts` page could fetch all posts during the build and pass them as `posts` metadata to the page component. It suggested changing the page component to accept `PostListMetadata` as props (`const Page: React.FC<PostListMetadata> = ({ posts }) => { ... }`) and said this would render a list of posts with links to their pages. This is incorrect: Next.js `generateMetadata` is for returning metadata, not for passing arbitrary data as page props.
